title: Breaking the System Noise Barrier at Exascale
problem: On exascale systems like El Capitan (1M+ CPU cores, 10K+ GPUs), OS and system services cause application interference, degrading performance and scalability
motivation: System noise at extreme scale directly impacts application performance; enabling scientific applications to leverage exascale hardware requires isolation strategies
method: The approach uses two complementary strategies. First, it isolates system services from applications using cgroup and systemd (Linux tools that control which CPU and memory resources each process can use), preventing them from interfering with each other. Second, it tunes the operating system itself—adjusting task scheduling and resource management—to reduce noise (unexpected delays and interruptions caused by system tasks). These tuning steps work on any Linux distribution, making them widely applicable.
key_novelty: This work is the first to document how system noise (interruptions from OS services) limits exascale systems like El Capitan (1M+ CPU cores, 10K+ GPUs), and provides tuning solutions that work on any Linux distribution.
contributions: Characterization of system noise at exascale (El Capitan)
System service isolation techniques reducing interference
OS-level tuning guide for general Linux systems
limitations: Abstract-only analysis; specific performance improvements not quantified; strategies may be system-dependent despite claimed distribution independence
